script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this script is inferred only from two-game form, not from the market. SF looks more likely to control flow: Purdy EPA/dropback is 0.38 unblitzed and 0.98 vs blitz (n=18), SF rushers are efficient (Black 21/90, CMC 20/91, Purdy 8/59), and SF blitzes 28% into an ARI QB at -0.31 EPA vs blitz (n=15) versus 0.13 unblitzed. Lean is SF ahead or neutral-positive, ARI pass-leaning through McBride (23 targets) with Wilson (14) and Bourne (11) well ahead of Harrison (4). Both backfields are committees, not bellcows.
script.flip1: ARI handles the blitz better than the n=15 sample and the game stays a neutral committee grind (Allgeier 22/71 and Love 20/70 vs Black/CMC near a 10-carry split). Team pass attempts fall toward the low 20s; Bourne still only needs about half his 43-yard pace, but a Harrison spike becomes less likely.
script.flip2: Shootout or SF's 4 explosives on 55 attempts doesn't travel: ARI airs it out, Harrison's 18.5 air yards/target finally connects and the under dies, while Bourne's short-area share (50 air yards on 11 targets) still cashes. Opposite flip is SF up big and ARI abandoning the run — that helps Bourne's over and only kills Harrison if his 6% target share rises, not merely if attempts rise.

matchup.overlap: ARI's primary option McBride (23 targets, 125 air yards, 136 rec yards) most likely attacks the middle, which is SF's tightest zone (5.75 YPA, n=8) — poor overlap, and his 69 line sits on his 68-yard pace, so he is not a leg. SF's Kittle (88 air, 92 yards) and Evans (95 air, 103 yards) overlap ARI's middle/right bleed, but their lines (47.5 and 55.5) sit at or above recent pace. Selected legs are role-vs-line: Bourne's 4.5 aDOT (50 air on 11 targets) is a short/intermediate profile that SF's 4/55 explosive cap does not erase, and Harrison's 74 air yards on 4 targets runs directly into that same explosive cap.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Bourne has 86 receiving yards on 11 targets over two games (about 43 yards and 5.5 targets a game, 4.5 aDOT), so a 23.5 line still clears if he loses nearly half that role, and SF's low explosive rate does not erase a short-area target.
edge_players.must_be_true: Kendrick Bourne targets >= 4 because he has 11 targets and 86 receiving yards over 2 games (7.8 yards per target), and 4 targets at that rate is about 31 yards versus a 23.5 line
edge_players.kills_it: IF Kendrick Bourne draws 2 or fewer targets THEN recyds over 23.5 fails

edge_players.edge_sentence: Harrison has 33 receiving yards on 4 targets over two games (about 16.5 yards a game) against a 33.5 line, a 6% share of ARI's 63 charted targets, and his 18.5 air yards per target runs into a SF defense that has allowed only 4 passes of 20+ on 55 attempts.
edge_players.must_be_true: Marvin Harrison Jr targets <= 3 because he has 4 targets and 33 receiving yards over 2 games (8.25 yards per target), and 3 targets at that rate is about 25 yards under the 33.5 line
edge_players.kills_it: IF Marvin Harrison Jr is targeted 5 or more times or catches one 35+ yard shot THEN recyds under 33.5 fails

data_check.notes: No projection, sim, or no-vig in the pack, so this check is pack-only. Bourne 43 yards/game vs a 23.5 line and Harrison 16.5 vs 33.5 both match the reads. SF allowed 4 passes of 20+ on 55 attempts, which supports the Harrison under and does not threaten Bourne's 50 air yards on 11 targets. SF blitz 28% plus ARI QB -0.31 EPA vs blitz is a passing-efficiency tax already small enough that a 23.5 rung still holds if Bourne keeps 4 targets; it is not a contradiction. Composite SF pass YPA is about 7.15. Nothing present cuts the strong Bourne read.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Bourne finished under 23.5 while Harrison cleared 33.5. Bourne's 86 yards came with 36 yards of YAC above 50 air yards, SF's 28% blitz (ARI QB -0.31 EPA vs blitz, n=15) funneled the quick game only to McBride, and Bourne's 11 targets were a two-game spike that Harrison's return to a normal share absorbed. Harrison, priced at 33.5 rather than his 16.5 pace, caught one deep shot — his entire two-game yardage total is 33 on 74 air yards, so a single 35-yard catch the 4-of-55 explosive rate does not forbid busts the under. The Harrison counter-case is real but not stronger than a 17-yard cushion plus the explosive cap, so the lean stays; if that one-play risk is unacceptable the Harrison leg is the one to drop, not Bourne.
slip_story: One ARI target-hierarchy stack, not a total or shootout stack: weeks 1-2 share holds (Bourne 11 of 63 charted targets, Harrison 4 of 63). Bourne over and Harrison under win together if that tree holds in either a trail script or a grind. Do not add McBride over 69 (line equals his 68-yard pace and he attacks SF's best zone), Wilson over 46.5 (37-yard pace, 74 yards on 133 air, SF explosive cap), or any SF rush leg that needs a different backfield story. No TDs, no receptions, no passing yards.
